# Sammappadhānavibhaṅga (Vb 8)

**ID:** Vb 8
**Section:** Vibhaṅga (vb)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sammappadhānavibhaṅga* is the eighth book or chapter of the *Vibhaṅga*, the second treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text is devoted to an analytical exposition of the four right strivings (*sammappadhāna*): the exertion to prevent unarisen unwholesome states, to abandon arisen unwholesome states, to arouse unarisen wholesome states, and to maintain and develop arisen wholesome states [Nyanatiloka 2007]. Its exposition includes a Suttanta analysis (*suttantabhājaniya*) providing the standard formula from the discourses followed by word-by-word definitions of its constituent terms [Nyanatiloka 2007; Gethin 2001]. In these definitions, the terms *vāyamati* ("strives"), *viriya* ("energy"), and *padahati* ("exerts") are explicated in identical terms that correspond to the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* register for *viriya*, while *chanda* is glossed as *kattukamyatā* ("desire to act"), representing its earliest formal Abhidhamma definition [Gethin 2001]. Later commentarial exegesis on the chapter is preserved in the *Sammohavinodanī* (*Vibh-a* 291–292) [Gethin 2001].

DharmaNexus identifies extensive textual reuse between the *Sammappadhānavibhaṅga* and other chapters of the *Vibhaṅga*, particularly the *Iddhipādavibhaṅga* (Vb 9), *Satipaṭṭhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 7), *Saccavibhaṅga* (Vb 4), and *Maggaṅgavibhaṅga* (Vb 11), as well as doctrinal parallels with the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* (*Tikanikkhepa*), the *Sammappadhāna Saṁyutta* (SN 49), the *Samaṇamuṇḍika Sutta* (MN 78), and sections of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 4 and AN 9) [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus identifies algorithmic alignments with various Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan texts treating the corresponding fourfold right exertion (*samyakprahāṇa* / *samyakpradhāna*), including the *Śrāvakabhūmi* of the *Yogācārabhūmi*, the *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, the *Dharmasaṃgraha*, the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99), and Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra* [DharmaNexus].
